question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.13(2)(b), a firm that establishes an interest-bearing common trust account for client funds must register the depository account information with the department, notify the department of any changes to that information, and furnish letters authorizing the department (and the department of administration) to audit the account.
choice_a: False — only the depository institution, not the firm, has any duty to notify the department
choice_b: True — the firm must register the account, report changes, and provide audit-authorization letters to the department
choice_c: False — audit authorization letters are required only if the board specifically requests them in writing
choice_d: False — the firm need only register the account once and has no ongoing duty to report changes
explanation: Wis. Stat. 452.13(2)(b) requires a firm maintaining an interest-bearing common trust account for client funds to register the depository account information with the department, notify the department of changes, and furnish letters authorizing the department and the department of administration to audit the account.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.13(2)(bm), after the department receives a firm's interest-bearing common trust account registration information, the department:
choice_a: Destroys the information after 30 days if no audit is initiated
choice_b: Publishes the information on a public registry
choice_c: Forwards that information to the department of administration
choice_d: Forwards the information to the firm's local county register of deeds
explanation: Wis. Stat. 452.13(2)(bm) provides that the department forwards the account registration information it receives under par. (b) to the department of administration, which is the beneficial owner of the interest earned.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.13(2)(c), a firm holding client funds must deposit:
choice_a: Only client funds exceeding $1,000 into the interest-bearing common trust account
choice_b: Client funds into whichever account type the client individually selects
choice_c: At least 50% of client funds into the interest-bearing common trust account
choice_d: All of the client funds it holds into the interest-bearing common trust account, with no partial exception
explanation: Wis. Stat. 452.13(2)(c) requires a firm to deposit all client funds into the interest-bearing common trust account described in the section; there is no statutory carve-out allowing partial deposit elsewhere.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.13(2)(e), when a depository institution remits interest to the department of administration, it must also furnish a statement showing the firm's name, the interest rate paid, any service charges or fees deducted, and the account balance.
choice_a: True — the statute requires that accompanying statement
choice_b: False — no accompanying statement is required, only the lump-sum remittance
choice_c: False — the statement is optional and left to the depository institution's discretion
choice_d: False — the statement need only show the account balance, nothing else
explanation: Wis. Stat. 452.13(2)(e) requires the depository institution to furnish a statement showing the firm's name, the applicable interest rate, the amount of service charges or fees deducted, and the account balance at the time of remittance.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.13(2)(f), besides being barred from deducting a service charge from the account's principal, a depository institution also may not:
choice_a: Refuse to open an interest-bearing common trust account for a licensed firm
choice_b: Assess a service charge against the firm personally or against the firm's other accounts, or charge the department of administration for maintaining the account
choice_c: Change the account's interest rate more than once per calendar year
choice_d: Require the firm to maintain a minimum balance in the account
explanation: In addition to the principal-deduction prohibition, Wis. Stat. 452.13(2)(f) bars a depository institution from assessing a service charge against the firm personally or against the firm's other accounts, and from charging the department of administration for the account.

question: Which of the following IS properly included within the statutory definition of "client funds" under Wis. Stat. 452.13(1)(a)?
choice_a: A promissory note given as part of a purchase offer
choice_b: A licensee's personal commission advance
choice_c: An earnest money deposit received by a licensee on behalf of a firm in connection with a conveyance of real estate
choice_d: A security deposit held by a licensee who personally owns the rental property
explanation: "Client funds" under Wis. Stat. 452.13(1)(a) means downpayments, earnest money deposits, or other money related to a conveyance of real estate received by a licensee on behalf of a firm or any other person; promissory notes are expressly excluded, and an owner-licensee's rental security deposit is governed separately under REEB 18.031(4).

question: Under REEB 18.02(5), a "real estate trust account" is defined as an account for real estate trust funds at a depository institution from which withdrawals or transfers are available without delay (subject to any required notice period), and the definition specifically includes:
choice_a: Only interest-bearing common trust accounts for client funds
choice_b: Only accounts held directly by the depository institution's trust department
choice_c: Only accounts denominated in the firm's own name without reference to any client
choice_d: Interest-bearing common trust accounts for client funds, non-interest-bearing accounts for real estate trust funds other than client funds, and interest-bearing accounts for real estate trust funds other than client funds
explanation: REEB 18.02(5) defines "real estate trust account" to include three types: interest-bearing common trust accounts for client funds, non-interest-bearing accounts for real estate trust funds other than client funds, and interest-bearing accounts for real estate trust funds other than client funds.

question: Under REEB 18.02(6), "real estate trust funds" is broadly defined to include cash, checks, share drafts, drafts, or notes received by a firm or licensee on behalf of a principal or other person, encompassing items such as:
choice_a: Land contract and mortgage payments, tax and insurance escrow payments, advance fees, rental deposits, security deposits, and earnest money downpayments
choice_b: Only earnest money downpayments connected to an offer to purchase
choice_c: Only funds physically delivered as cash, excluding checks or drafts
choice_d: Only funds held for commercial (non-residential) transactions
explanation: REEB 18.02(6) defines "real estate trust funds" expansively to include, among other items, land contract and mortgage payments, tax and insurance escrow payments, advance fees, rental application deposits and rents, security deposits, and earnest money downpayments.

question: Under REEB 18.02(6)(a), which of the following is expressly listed as "real estate trust funds"?
choice_a: A licensee's continuing education tuition reimbursement
choice_b: Land contract payments and mortgage payments received on behalf of a principal
choice_c: A firm's general liability insurance premium
choice_d: A licensee's personal automobile lease payment
explanation: REEB 18.02(6)(a) lists land contract payments and mortgage payments received on behalf of a principal as real estate trust funds subject to trust account handling.

question: Under REEB 18.02(6)(b), which category of funds received by a firm is treated as "real estate trust funds"?
choice_a: A referral fee paid between two cooperating brokers
choice_b: A licensee's board-imposed forfeiture payment
choice_c: Tax and insurance escrow payments
choice_d: A firm's franchise royalty payment
explanation: REEB 18.02(6)(b) identifies tax and insurance escrow payments received by a firm as real estate trust funds.

question: Under REEB 18.02(6)(c), an advance fee or finder's fee collected by a firm is treated as "real estate trust funds":
choice_a: Only if it exceeds $500
choice_b: Only if the client is a first-time buyer
choice_c: Never — advance fees are always excluded from trust fund treatment
choice_d: Unless the fee is non-refundable
explanation: REEB 18.02(6)(c) lists advance fees and finder's fees as real estate trust funds unless the fee is non-refundable, in which case the fee falls outside the trust-fund definition.

question: Under REEB 18.02(6)(e), funds received by a firm for repayment to a third party are treated as:
choice_a: Real estate trust funds
choice_b: The firm's operating revenue
choice_c: A non-depositable item automatically
choice_d: Client funds subject to the interest-bearing common trust account rules only
explanation: REEB 18.02(6)(e) lists funds received by a firm or licensee for repayment to a third party among the categories of real estate trust funds.

question: Under REEB 18.02(6)(g), which of the following is expressly listed as real estate trust funds?
choice_a: A licensee's continuing education course fee
choice_b: Initial and additional earnest money downpayments connected with an offer to purchase, option, or exchange agreement
choice_c: A buyer's home inspection fee paid directly to the inspector
choice_d: A firm's errors-and-omissions insurance premium
explanation: REEB 18.02(6)(g) lists initial and additional earnest money downpayments and related funds connected with an offer to purchase, option, or exchange agreement as real estate trust funds.

question: Under REEB 18.031(2), a licensee (as opposed to the firm) who personally receives real estate trust funds must:
choice_a: Deposit the funds directly into the firm's real estate trust account under the licensee's own signature authority, bypassing the firm
choice_b: Hold the funds personally until closing, then remit them to the firm
choice_c: Promptly submit the funds to the firm
choice_d: Deposit the funds into the licensee's personal bank account for safekeeping
explanation: REEB 18.031(2) requires a licensee who receives real estate trust funds to promptly submit those funds to the firm, which then bears the deposit obligations under REEB 18.031(1).

question: Under REEB 18.031(5), instead of depositing rental application deposits, rents, and security deposits into the firm's real estate trust account, a firm managing rental property may:
choice_a: Deposit those funds into the firm's operating account so long as a separate ledger is kept
choice_b: Hold those funds as cash in the firm's safe until the lease terminates
choice_c: Forward those funds directly to the tenant's own bank account
choice_d: Deposit those funds directly into an account maintained in the name of the property owner, with a licensee authorized as signatory as directed by the owner
explanation: REEB 18.031(5) permits a firm to deposit rental application deposits, rents, and security deposits directly into an account maintained in the name of the property owner, with a licensee authorized as a signatory on that account as directed by the owner.

question: Under REEB 18.033(1), if a firm receives real estate trust funds, the firm:
choice_a: Shall open a real estate trust account
choice_b: May choose instead to route the funds through an attorney's trust account
choice_c: May hold the funds in the firm's operating account for up to 30 days before opening a trust account
choice_d: Is required to open a trust account only if the funds exceed $5,000
explanation: REEB 18.033(1) requires that a firm shall open a real estate trust account if the firm receives real estate trust funds.

question: Under REEB 18.033(2), a firm may close a real estate trust account:
choice_a: At any time regardless of whether trust funds remain in the account, provided the department is not notified
choice_b: If no real estate trust funds remain in the account, or for reasons specified in REEB 18.035
choice_c: Only with prior written approval of every client with funds on deposit
choice_d: Only at the end of the firm's fiscal year
explanation: REEB 18.033(2) permits a firm to close a real estate trust account if no real estate trust funds remain in the account, or for reasons specified in REEB 18.035.

question: Under REEB 18.035(2), a firm must notify the department no later than 10 days after which of the following events?
choice_a: Any single deposit into the account exceeding $10,000
choice_b: Hiring a new bookkeeper to reconcile the account
choice_c: Changing the trust account's name or number, changing the depository institution, closing the account, or converting the account to or from an interest-bearing common trust account for client funds
choice_d: The account earning more interest than the prior calendar year
explanation: REEB 18.035(2) requires a firm to notify the department no later than 10 days after changing a real estate trust account's name or number, changing depository institutions, closing an account, or converting the account to or from an interest-bearing common trust account established for client funds.

question: Under REEB 18.06, when the parties to a transaction designate an escrow agent other than the firm to hold earnest money, the firm itself is:
choice_a: Required to co-sign the escrow agreement as guarantor
choice_b: Permitted to hold the funds so long as it notifies the department within 10 days
choice_c: Required to deposit a matching amount of its own funds as a surety
choice_d: Prohibited from holding the funds in its real estate trust account or otherwise serving as custodian of the funds
explanation: REEB 18.06 provides that when the parties designate an escrow agent other than the firm, the firm may not hold the funds in its real estate trust account or otherwise serve as custodian of the funds for the parties.

question: Under REEB 18.06, when parties designate an escrow agent other than the firm, permissible third-party escrow agents identified in the rule include:
choice_a: A bank, a savings and loan association, a credit union, or an attorney
choice_b: Only a title insurance company
choice_c: Only a licensed real estate broker from a different firm
choice_d: Only the county register of deeds
explanation: REEB 18.06 identifies a bank, a savings and loan association, a credit union, or an attorney as permissible third-party escrow agents when the parties do not want the firm holding the earnest money.

question: Under REEB 18.07(1), an agreement to hold funds in escrow after closing (until some future occurrence) must be prepared by the parties or an attorney, except that a licensee MAY draft such an agreement if:
choice_a: The amount held in escrow is under $1,000
choice_b: A form for that purpose has been approved by the board for licensee use under REEB 16.03
choice_c: Both parties are represented by the same firm
choice_d: The licensee has at least 10 years of experience
explanation: REEB 18.07(1) allows a licensee to draft an after-closing escrow agreement only if a form for that purpose has been approved by the board for licensee use under REEB 16.03; otherwise the agreement must be prepared by the parties or an attorney.

question: Under REEB 18.07(2), a firm may hold certain post-closing funds in its real estate trust account WITHOUT a separate escrow agreement, provided the closing statement indicates the firm is holding the funds, for items such as:
choice_a: Any funds at all, regardless of type, so long as both parties orally agree
choice_b: The firm's own earned commission pending a dispute
choice_c: Occupancy or possession escrows, escrows for final proration of taxes, and escrows for charges incurred by a seller but not yet billed
choice_d: A buyer's full purchase price pending a title search
explanation: REEB 18.07(2) allows a firm to hold occupancy or possession escrows, escrows for final proration of taxes, and escrows for charges incurred by a seller but not yet billed, without a separate escrow agreement, as long as the closing statement indicates the firm is holding the funds.

question: Under REEB 18.09(1), a firm that disburses trust funds under the circumstances enumerated in the rule avoids violating which statute?
choice_a: Wis. Stat. 452.03, the licensure requirement statute
choice_b: Wis. Stat. 452.23, the recovery fund statute
choice_c: Wis. Stat. 452.137, the education requirements statute
choice_d: Wis. Stat. 452.14(3)(i), the "demonstrated incompetency" ground for discipline
explanation: REEB 18.09(1) provides that a firm disbursing trust funds under the circumstances it enumerates does not violate Wis. Stat. 452.14(3)(i), which authorizes discipline for demonstrated incompetency in a manner that safeguards the interests of the public.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code REEB 18.09(1); Wis. Stat. 452.14(3)(i)

question: Under REEB 18.09(1)(a), a firm may properly return earnest money to the payer when:
choice_a: An offer, lease, exchange agreement, or option is rejected, expires, or is withdrawn before there is a binding acceptance
choice_b: The seller simply asks for the funds back after closing
choice_c: 30 days have passed since the offer was signed, regardless of its status
choice_d: The buyer's financing is merely delayed but the offer remains binding
explanation: REEB 18.09(1)(a) permits a firm to return funds to the payer when an offer, lease, exchange agreement, or option is rejected, expires, or is withdrawn before there is a binding acceptance.

question: Under REEB 18.09(1)(b), a firm may disburse trust funds as directed in a written earnest money disbursement agreement signed by all interested parties; the rule specifically notes that:
choice_a: The agreement must be separately notarized to be valid
choice_b: A closing statement can itself qualify as such a written disbursement agreement
choice_c: Only the buyer's signature is required, not the seller's
choice_d: Such an agreement is valid only if drafted by an attorney
explanation: REEB 18.09(1)(b) allows disbursement as directed in a written earnest money disbursement agreement signed by all interested parties, and expressly notes that a closing statement qualifies as such an agreement.

question: Under REEB 18.09(1)(c) and (d), a firm may properly disburse trust funds by:
choice_a: Paying the funds to whichever party's attorney contacts the firm first
choice_b: Splitting the funds evenly between the parties without further authorization
choice_c: Paying the funds into a court with jurisdiction over a civil action involving all interested parties, or by following a court order
choice_d: Transferring the funds to the listing broker's operating account pending mediation
explanation: REEB 18.09(1)(c) and (d) authorize a firm to disburse trust funds by paying them into a court with jurisdiction over a civil action involving all interested parties, or by following a court order.

question: Under REEB 18.09(1)(e), a firm may disburse trust funds on the advice of an attorney if:
choice_a: The attorney represents the buyer only
choice_b: The advice is given verbally by any attorney the firm regularly uses
choice_c: The attorney is a member of the firm's brokerage
choice_d: The attorney does not represent any party to the contract and gives the advice in good faith
explanation: REEB 18.09(1)(e) permits disbursement on the advice of an attorney who does not represent any party to the contract, given in good faith.

question: Under REEB 18.09(1)(f) and (g), a firm may also properly disburse trust funds by:
choice_a: Acting pursuant to authorization contained within the contract itself, or in compliance with other applicable law
choice_b: Following the verbal instruction of the listing agent's broker only
choice_c: Waiting until the licensee's license renews, then disbursing automatically
choice_d: Relying on an unwritten industry custom
explanation: REEB 18.09(1)(f) and (g) authorize disbursement pursuant to authorization contained in the contract, or in compliance with other applicable law.

question: Under REEB 18.09(2), the 30-day written notice by certified mail before disbursement is required specifically when a firm intends to disburse under REEB 18.09(1)(a) and the parties disagree about the rejection, expiration, or withdrawal, OR when disbursing under REEB 18.09(1)(e), (f), or (g) and there is disagreement among the parties.
choice_a: False — the 30-day notice applies to every disbursement without exception
choice_b: True — the notice requirement is tied to those specific disagreement scenarios
choice_c: False — the notice requirement applies only to disbursements under a court order
choice_d: False — no notice is ever required if the amount in dispute is under $1,000
explanation: REEB 18.09(2) ties the certified-mail, 30-day notice requirement to disbursements under par. (1)(a) where the parties disagree about the rejection, expiration, or withdrawal, and to disbursements under par. (1)(e), (f), or (g) where there is disagreement among the parties.

question: Under REEB 18.10(1), aside from the limited $300 personal-funds exception, a firm's real estate trust account:
choice_a: May contain the firm's general operating funds so long as they are tracked separately in the ledger
choice_b: May contain a licensee's personal savings if the licensee is also the broker of record
choice_c: Shall contain only real estate trust funds
choice_d: May contain funds from unrelated business ventures owned by the firm's principals
explanation: REEB 18.10(1) establishes the baseline commingling prohibition: a firm shall deposit only real estate trust funds in the firm's real estate trust account, subject only to the narrow $300 personal-funds exception in par. (1)(b).

question: Under REEB 18.13, the introductory provision requires each firm to maintain and be responsible for a bookkeeping system:
choice_a: At any location the firm's accountant chooses, with no minimum required components
choice_b: Only if the firm's trust account balance exceeds $50,000
choice_c: Solely through the firm's depository institution's own record-keeping service
choice_d: In the firm's office, consisting of at least the components enumerated in the rule (journal, ledger, reconciliation, trial balance, and validation)
explanation: REEB 18.13 requires each firm to maintain and be responsible for a bookkeeping system in the firm's office consisting of at least the components enumerated in the rule: a cash journal, a ledger, monthly account reconciliation, a trial balance, and validation.

question: Under REEB 18.13(1)(c), the cash journal must identify each transaction by including at least:
choice_a: The name of the principal and an identification number or other means of identification linking the journal to the corresponding ledger transaction
choice_b: The principal's Social Security number
choice_c: The licensee's individual license number only
choice_d: The buyer's mortgage lender's name
explanation: REEB 18.13(1)(c) requires the journal to identify each transaction by including at least the name of the principal and an identification number or other means of identification linking the journal to the corresponding transaction and ledger.

question: Under REEB 18.13(1)(d), the cash journal must also include:
choice_a: A running balance updated only at month's end
choice_b: A running balance for each day on which receipts or disbursements are entered
choice_c: A separate journal for each licensee employed by the firm
choice_d: The firm's total annual gross commission income
explanation: REEB 18.13(1)(d) requires the journal to include a running balance for each day on which receipts or disbursements are entered.

question: Under REEB 18.13(2), the "ledger" component of a firm's bookkeeping system is used to:
choice_a: Track only the firm's marketing expenditures for each listing
choice_b: Record only disbursements, since receipts are tracked exclusively in the journal
choice_c: Record the receipts and disbursements as they affect each particular transaction, with entries including the names of all parties, dates, amounts, and a running, segregated balance
choice_d: Summarize the firm's annual tax filings
explanation: REEB 18.13(2) requires the ledger to record receipts and disbursements as they affect each particular transaction, with entries that include the names of all parties, dates, amounts received, and disbursement details, along with a running balance that segregates each transaction.

question: Under REEB 18.13(2), a firm must maintain separate ledgers or separate ledger sections for:
choice_a: Each individual licensee affiliated with the firm, regardless of transaction type
choice_b: Each calendar quarter of the fiscal year
choice_c: Each depository institution used by the firm, combined across transaction types
choice_d: Each of the various kinds of real estate transactions, such as sales, rental collections, and mortgage or land contract collections
explanation: REEB 18.13(2) requires the firm to maintain a separate ledger, or a separate section of the ledger, for each of the various kinds of real estate transactions, including sales, rental collections, or mortgage and land contract collections.

question: Under REEB 18.13(4), the "trial balance" is best described as:
choice_a: A written listing, prepared in conjunction with the account reconciliation, of all open items in the real estate trust account, showing the parties and the amount held in trust for each
choice_b: A one-time balance calculated only when a trust account is first opened
choice_c: The firm's projected annual commission income
choice_d: A summary of disciplinary complaints filed against the firm
explanation: REEB 18.13(4) requires the firm to prepare a written listing, called the "trial balance," of all open items in the real estate trust account, including the names of all parties and the amount held in trust, prepared in conjunction with the monthly reconciliation.

question: Under REEB 18.13(4), instead of listing the names of the parties to a transaction on the trial balance, a firm may:
choice_a: Omit the entry entirely if the transaction closed within the same month
choice_b: Substitute the ledger page number or other means of identification from the ledger to label the funds
choice_c: List only the depository institution's internal account code
choice_d: List only the licensee's name who handled the transaction
explanation: REEB 18.13(4) allows a firm to substitute the ledger page number or other means of identification from the ledger in lieu of the parties' names when labeling the funds on the trial balance.

question: Under REEB 18.13(5), the "validation" step requires the firm or a designated person to:
choice_a: Have the trust account audited by an outside CPA at least once per year
choice_b: File the trial balance with the department within 10 days
choice_c: Review the reconciled account statement balance, the open ledger account listing, and the journal running balance to ensure all of these records are valid and in agreement
choice_d: Obtain a client signature confirming the ending balance
explanation: REEB 18.13(5) requires the firm or a designated person to review the reconciled account statement balance, the open ledger account listing (trial balance), and the journal running balance to ensure all three records are valid and in agreement as of the reconciliation date.

question: Under REEB 18.13(6), a firm may use a computerized system to maintain its bookkeeping records provided:
choice_a: The system is certified annually by the depository institution
choice_b: Only a licensed CPA is permitted to operate the software
choice_c: The firm first obtains board pre-approval of the specific software product used
choice_d: The computerized system fully complies with the journal, ledger, reconciliation, trial balance, and validation requirements of REEB 18.13(1) to (5)
explanation: REEB 18.13(6)(a) permits use of a computerized bookkeeping system so long as it complies fully with subs. (1) to (5) — the journal, ledger, reconciliation, trial balance, and validation requirements.

question: Under REEB 18.13(6)(c), if a firm uses a computerized bookkeeping system, a backup copy of the journal and ledger records must be made:
choice_a: On any day entries are made in the computerized system, on a medium separate and distinct from the source documents
choice_b: Only once per calendar quarter, on any available medium
choice_c: Only when the firm changes depository institutions
choice_d: Only if the firm's office lacks a fireproof safe
explanation: REEB 18.13(6)(c) requires a backup copy of the journal and ledger records to be made on any day on which entries are made in the computerized system, on a disk or other medium separate and distinct from that on which the source documents reside.

question: Under REEB 18.13(6)(d), after the firm completes the monthly reconciliation, trial balance, and validation, the resulting documents must be:
choice_a: Mailed to the department within 5 business days
choice_b: Immediately copied to a backup medium and maintained by the broker
choice_c: Shredded once the reconciliation is confirmed accurate
choice_d: Retained only in the original computer file, with no backup required
explanation: REEB 18.13(6)(d) requires that after complying with subs. (3) to (5), the document recording the account reconciliation, trial balance, and validation be immediately copied to a backup medium and maintained by the broker.

question: Under REEB 18.13(6)(e), computerized trust account records must be made available for inspection and copying by the department, and exact and complete copies must be:
choice_a: Sent to the department only after the firm is compensated for reproduction costs
choice_b: Provided only during a scheduled annual audit, never on an ad hoc request
choice_c: Promptly sent to the department upon request, without charge to the department or board
choice_d: Provided only if the request is accompanied by a subpoena
explanation: REEB 18.13(6)(e) requires that all records be made available for inspection and copying by the department, with exact and complete copies promptly sent to the department upon request, without charge to the department or board, for purposes of an audit or investigation.

question: Under REEB 18.13(6)(f), computerized real estate trust account records must be retained:
choice_a: For a shorter period than paper trust records, since electronic storage is considered less reliable
choice_b: Indefinitely, with no permitted destruction date
choice_c: Only for as long as the computer hardware on which they were created remains in service
choice_d: Pursuant to REEB 15.04, the same records-retention rule that applies to a firm's other transaction records
explanation: REEB 18.13(6)(f) requires that all computerized trust account records be retained pursuant to REEB 15.04, applying the same retention period as the firm's other transaction records.

question: Under REEB 15.02(3), when a lease or rental agreement has been accepted and signed by all parties, the broker or salesperson must promptly distribute an exact and complete copy of it to:
choice_a: The tenant, upon execution
choice_b: Only the landlord, since the landlord is the firm's client
choice_c: Only the property management department of the firm
choice_d: No one, unless a party specifically requests a copy
explanation: REEB 15.02(3) requires a broker or salesperson to promptly distribute an exact and complete copy of a lease or rental agreement that has been accepted and signed by all parties to the tenant, upon execution.

question: Under REEB 15.02(4), when a listing contract or agency agreement has been accepted and signed by all parties, the broker or salesperson must promptly distribute an exact and complete copy of it to:
choice_a: Only the department, for its files
choice_b: The client
choice_c: Only the cooperating broker in the transaction
choice_d: No one until the listing expires
explanation: REEB 15.02(4) requires a broker or salesperson to promptly distribute an exact and complete copy of a listing contract or agency agreement that has been accepted and signed by all parties to the client.

question: Under REEB 15.04(2), a licensee associated with a firm who has transaction documents subject to the retention requirement must:
choice_a: Retain the documents personally for 2 years and only forward them to the firm if requested
choice_b: Forward the documents directly to the department instead of the firm
choice_c: Promptly submit those documents to the firm
choice_d: Destroy personal copies immediately after closing, since only the firm's copy matters
explanation: REEB 15.04(2) requires an associated licensee to promptly submit transaction documents to the firm so the firm can satisfy its recordkeeping and retention obligations.

question: Under REEB 15.04(1), the standard 2-year retention period for a firm's transaction records may run longer than 2 years when:
choice_a: The transaction involved a first-time homebuyer
choice_b: The firm's broker of record has held a license for more than 20 years
choice_c: The property sold for more than $1 million
choice_d: Retention is required by federal law, or the records are needed for an active board investigation
explanation: REEB 15.04(1) sets a baseline 2-year retention period, but records must be retained longer where required by federal law or where they are needed for an active board investigation.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.42(2), which body determines the specific transaction documents or records a licensee must retain?
choice_a: The board (Real Estate Examining Board), through rules it promulgates
choice_b: Each individual depository institution
choice_c: The Wisconsin Department of Revenue
choice_d: Each firm's malpractice insurance carrier
explanation: Wis. Stat. 452.42(2) provides that a licensee shall retain documents or records related to a transaction, as determined by the board, in accordance with rules promulgated by the board (implemented through REEB 15.04).

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.42(1), the term "electronic" (as used in the records-retention statute permitting electronic file formats) is defined by reference to which other statute?
choice_c: Wis. Stat. 706.01
choice_d: Wis. Stat. 895.01
explanation: Wis. Stat. 452.42(1) defines "electronic" by cross-reference to the definition given in Wis. Stat. 137.11(5), part of Wisconsin's Uniform Electronic Transactions Act.

question: A firm receives an earnest money check on a Tuesday, along with a promissory note the buyer offered as part of the same purchase offer. Under Wis. Stat. 452.13(1)(a) and REEB 18.031(1), which item must the firm deposit into its real estate trust account within 48 hours?
choice_a: Both the check and the note, since both were offered as part of the same purchase offer
choice_b: Neither item, since a promissory note voids the trust deposit requirement for the whole offer
choice_c: The earnest money check only — the promissory note is excluded from the definition of client funds and is not depositable in the same way
choice_d: The promissory note only, since notes are considered higher-risk instruments requiring faster handling
explanation: Because promissory notes are expressly excluded from the statutory definition of "client funds" under Wis. Stat. 452.13(1)(a), the 48-hour trust-deposit obligation under REEB 18.031(1) applies to the earnest money check; a promissory note is instead handled as a non-depositable item under REEB 18.11, subject to an escrow agreement.
source_note: Wis. Stat. 452.13(1)(a); Wis. Admin. Code REEB 18.031(1), 18.11

question: A firm's property management division holds tenant security deposits for properties it manages for outside owners (the firm itself has no ownership interest). Under REEB 18.02(6)(f) and 18.031, these security deposits are:
choice_a: Exempt from all trust fund handling requirements because they are held for outside owners
choice_b: Treated the same as a licensee-owned rental property's deposits under REEB 18.031(4)
choice_c: Automatically classified as non-depositable items under REEB 18.11
choice_d: Real estate trust funds that generally must be handled under the firm's trust account rules, subject to the direct owner-account option in REEB 18.031(5)
explanation: Security deposits on rental property are listed as real estate trust funds under REEB 18.02(6)(f); when the firm (not a licensee-owner) manages the property for an outside owner, the deposits are generally handled under the trust account and deposit rules, with REEB 18.031(5) offering the option of direct deposit into an owner-named account. REEB 18.031(4) applies specifically where the licensee personally holds an ownership interest in the rental property.
